sources.title: Vatén et al. (2011), Callose biosynthesis regulates symplastic trafficking during root development
sources.supports: Opened primary abstract: Arabidopsis CALS3 gain of function increases callose at PD, decreases aperture and reduces intercellular traffic.

sources.title: In situ architecture of plasmodesmata in Physcomitrium patens resolved by cryo-electron tomography (2026)
sources.supports: Opened full text, Results and Fig. 2: plasma membrane lines the wall cavity; callose-rich material belongs to cell wall around necks. Used for membrane/wall boundary, not moss-specific closure kinetics in Arabidopsis.

sources.title: Nicolas et al. (2017), Architecture and permeability of post-cytokinesis plasmodesmata lacking cytoplasmic sleeves
sources.supports: Opened primary abstract: ER-PM separation and tethers depend on differentiation; a widened sleeve is one structural state, not all plasmodesmata.

findings.evidence: At p=.6 and p=1, gate=callose, actual cytosolic-leaflet vertex 649 is [0.6625000238,0.7549144030,-0.2841519415]. A ray from it intersects the actual right collar triangles once, proving it is inside the closed collar solid; nearest collar triangle is 0.0747897835 away. At p=.35 it is outside. Torus thickening to .52 is incompatible with the independent |x/1.06|^5 neck profile.
findings.whyWrong: Callose is wall-side material. A continuous plasma membrane must remain the boundary between it and the cytoplasmic sleeve. The generated callose collar engulfs the membrane on its flanks and occupies part of the sleeve, contrary to the stage text and depicted topology.
findings.fix: Use one coupled neck profile for wall-facing callose surface and both membrane leaflets so the thickening displaces the entire membrane profile without crossing it; retain the open central sleeve and both cargo outcomes.
findings.verification: Sweep callose progress and actual collar/membrane surfaces, including the flank witness near x=.6625. No cytosolic-leaflet surface point may lie inside callose; no triangle intersections. Retain first-particle passage, later blockage, bulky-cargo exclusion, deterministic seeks and resource stability.

limits: Transforms and deformation are continuous; the hard stop for late cargo is an intentional exclusion boundary, not a demonstrated teleport.
The topology finding is static during late callose accumulation, not evidence of a dropped animation frame.

limitations: No browser or rendered continuous-playback acceptance was performed; root owns that gate.

sources.title: Boldt et al. (2005), D-GLYCERATE 3-KINASE, the Last Unknown Enzyme in the Photorespiratory Cycle in Arabidopsis
sources.supports: Opened full text: two 2C substrates yield a 3C product and CO2, via chloroplast/peroxisome/mitochondrial steps; chloroplastic GLYK completes glycerate phosphorylation; knockout accumulates glycerate.

sources.title: Perkins et al. (1997), Electron tomography of neuronal mitochondria: three-dimensional structure and organization of cristae and membrane contacts
sources.supports: Opened primary abstract: cristae are invaginations of the inner membrane connected through narrow crista junctions. Used only for conserved inner-membrane continuity, not neuronal dimensions or plant-specific architecture.

findings.evidence: The helper creates ten short cylinder necks. Eight complete actual neck meshes lie strictly inside a sphere that itself lies inside every triangle of the inner-envelope mesh, so they cannot meet that envelope. Inner-envelope triangle inradius is 0.9970928723 in inner-membrane local coordinates; central neck 5 has maximum rendered vertex radius 0.8516170022, leaving at least 0.1454758702 separation. This is a whole-mesh bounding proof, not nearest-vertex distance or userData. See evidence/plantConnections/diagnostic.json cristae.
findings.whyWrong: Normal cristae are continuous invaginations of the inner boundary membrane. The explicitly constructed necks instead terminate freely in the matrix, contradicting their intended structural role. This is independent of otherwise correct carbon chemistry.
findings.fix: Derive each crista junction/neck endpoint from the actual inner-envelope surface, with attached membrane/lumen contours; keep connections confined to inner membrane and preserve the double-envelope separation. Update the owned shared anatomy helper for both affected models.
findings.verification: Measure actual rendered neck-to-inner-envelope attachment for all ten junctions in photorespiration and CAM after transforms; original central-neck geometry must fail. Check the full crista contour and lumen continuity, no outer-envelope crossing, finite geometry and stable resources.

limits: No demonstrated carbon-position jump; bond identity changes and coproduct appearance are schematic chemistry events.
Transporter-level membrane passage and reaction-center atomic geometry are not resolved; no claim that the cutaway routes are complete physical transport simulations.

models.scope: Maize main NADP-ME C4 branch versus mature Kalanchoe fedtschenkoi mitochondrial NAD-ME CAM branch; strategy=c4/cam; full 0–1 interval.
checks: PEPC acts in mesophyll cytosol with a 3C acceptor plus one incoming carbon. C4 oxaloacetate-to-malate waypoint lies in mesophyll chloroplast section, malate crosses the outbound symplastic pore, CO2 releases near bundle-sheath chloroplast, 3C pyruvate returns through a distinct pore for PPDK regeneration.
Independently swept 1001 C4 frames using actual carbon positions and radii against drawn torus/pore/desmotubule parameters; checked complete particle radius, not center alone.

CAM nocturnal capture precedes vacuolar storage (.32–.49); day transition .47–.57 closes guard-cell inset; mitochondrial malate decarboxylation precedes movement of released carbon toward chloroplast. Mature-leaf NAD-ME evidence is specific to K. fedtschenkoi.

Read both languages: intro, six stages, C4 and CAM labels, strategy options, entry summary, sources. Additional C4 routes and four-phase CAM complexity are explicitly omitted; no generic-plant universal claim.
Measured owned helper's actual CAM mitochondrial necks and confirmed same structural defect as photorespiration.
Smoke passes both branches; 412 visible-transform samples each, deterministic arbitrary seeks, stable inventories. Hidden alternate branch excluded from visible-motion interpretation.
